name: Last week of the giveaway
notes: Seven slideshows for the week of October 26, the last week of the giveaway (ends Oct 31). Two new: the giveaway push (20, best posted early in the week while there are the most entries left to earn) and the app sell, "Answers for the questions you live with" (21). Five carried over unposted from the good days set, keeping their numbers: tips 2, 3 and 4, harder than cardio, and the dictionary’s volume 2.

creatives.name: Last week of the giveaway
creatives.title: Last week to win an Apple Watch, and I'm giving away all of this 🩵
creatives.goal: Urgency. Every prize gets its own slide, then how to still get entries in before Oct 31.
creatives.caption: It's the last week of my Dysautonomia Awareness Month giveaway 🩵 Up for grabs: an Apple Watch Series 12 (iPhone grand prize), a Polar H10 (Android grand prize), 4 Coospo heart-rate straps, 10 boxes of LMNT and 25 free years of Autonomic Pro. How to enter: download Autonomic (free on iOS & Android, link in bio), sign up on the giveaway card in the Journal, and take an HRV reading each morning. Your phone's camera works. One entry per day you take a reading, up to 10, through Oct 31. Tag a friend who needs this for a bonus entry 👇 Winners drawn Nov 1. US residents 18+, no purchase necessary. Your health data stays on your phone. Not affiliated with TikTok, Apple, Polar, Coospo or LMNT. #giveaway #pots #longcovid #dysautonomia #dysautonomiaawarenessmonth

creatives.name: Answers for the questions you live with
creatives.title: The 5 questions every POTS patient asks every single day
creatives.goal: Sell the app hard. Each question is one people ask themselves every day, and each answer is a real screen.
creatives.caption: Answers for the questions you live with 🩵 I asked myself these every day for years, so I built Autonomic to answer them from my own numbers: HRV, heart rate, sleep and symptoms. Free on iOS & Android (link in bio). Your phone's camera is enough to start, and every feature is free for 14 days. Your data never leaves your phone. Which question do you ask most? 👇 #pots #dysautonomia #longcovid #mecfs #chronicillness #hrv #pacing

text: 5 questions I asked myself *every single day* with POTS.
And an app I built that answers them.

img.shows: You sitting on the edge of the bed in the morning, phone in hand, looking at it. Tired but not staged.
img.frame: Face in the upper third; the hook across the middle under a dark wash.

text: 1. Is today going to be a *good day?*
One score every morning, from my own HRV, sleep and heart rate.

img.shows: The Journal home: Outlook card with the Autonomic score, pacing strip and key figures.
img.frame: Raw full-height screenshot from the top.

text: 2. How much can I do *before I crash?*
A pacing budget in minutes, fitted to me. It warns me before I go over.

img.shows: The Journal home with the pacing strip (1h 21m left of 3h 35m).
img.frame: Raw full-height screenshot; the strip in the top two thirds.

text: 3. Is it really this bad, or am I *overreacting?*
12 weeks of stand tests, on one chart. Proof I can hand my doctor.

img.shows: Progress, POTS section: 12 weeks of stand tests, 12 of 12 over the threshold.
img.frame: Raw full-height screenshot, the chart in the top two thirds.

text: 4. Is anything I take *actually helping?*
It checks my meds, supplements and habits against my own numbers.

img.shows: NEW SCREENSHOT NEEDED: the Insights tab with a correlation row like "Magnesium days show higher RMSSD", or the Biggest change card.
img.frame: Raw full-height screenshot, the finding in the top two thirds.

text: 5. Am I *about to crash?*
When my numbers start sliding, it tells me. Usually days before I feel it.

img.shows: Your HRV trend dropping over several days.
img.frame: Raw full-height screenshot, the falling line in the top two thirds.

creatives.name: Tip 2: legs up the wall
creatives.title: POTS tip #2: put your legs up the wall for 10 minutes
creatives.goal: Second single tip. Something people can do tonight.
creatives.caption: POTS tip #2. Ten minutes, zero equipment 🩵 Not medical advice, ask your doctor what's right for you. #pots #potstips #dysautonomia #pacing #spoonie

text: POTS tip #2:
*Legs up the wall.* 10 minutes. That's the whole tip.

img.shows: Someone lying on the floor with their legs up a plain wall, shot from the side or showing legs only. No face.
img.frame: Legs and wall fill the frame; the tip sits over the darkened middle.

text: Gravity pulls blood into my legs all day.
For ten minutes, *I make it work for me.*
slides.fine: Not medical advice. Ask your doctor what's right for you.

img.shows: Feet in socks resting high on a wall, soft indoor light. No face.
img.frame: Feet in the top third; copy across the lower half.

text: In the app I built, resting like this *buys back time* on my pacing budget.
Link in bio. 🩵

img.shows: The Journal home with the pacing strip (1h 21m left of 3h 35m). Better: a day with a legs-up entry logged, so the strip shows minutes bought back.
img.frame: Pacing strip level with the copy.

music.notes: Same sound family as tip #1 so the series is recognisable. Slow and restful: this one is about lying down.

creatives.name: Harder than cardio
creatives.title: Things that spike my heart rate more than a workout
creatives.goal: Funny list that doubles as awareness. Ends on proof.
creatives.caption: I am not out of shape, my nervous system is just dramatic 😅🩵 #pots #dysautonomia #chronicillnesshumor #longcovid #spoonie

text: Things that spike my heart rate *more than a workout.*

img.shows: A laundry basket half folded, sitting on a bed or couch. No people.
img.frame: Basket in the lower half, hook above it.

text: 1. Standing in line
2. A hot shower
3. Folding laundry
4. Tying a tiny shoe
5. The stairs. Just the stairs.

img.shows: A plain indoor staircase, looking up.
img.frame: Darkened about 85% under the list.

text: I'm not out of shape. *I have the receipts.*
Free app in bio to record yours. 🩵

img.shows: A POTS Test result: sustained HR rise +45 bpm (bad), the heart rate trace jumping at the stand, baseline 66, peak 118.
img.frame: The +45 and the trace beside the copy.

music.notes: The joke is the mismatch: gym-montage intensity over folding laundry. An over-the-top motivational or training beat, played straight. Drop to something softer on the last slide if the sound allows.

creatives.name: Tip 3: on a good day, do half
creatives.title: POTS tip #3: on a good day, do half
creatives.goal: Third single tip. The pacing one, and the most natural lead into the app.
creatives.caption: POTS tip #3, and the one that took me longest to learn 🩵 Good days are where crashes are made. #pots #pacing #mecfs #longcovid #dysautonomia

text: POTS tip #3:
On a good day, *do half* of what you think you can.

img.search: to do list notebook half crossed off
img.shows: A handwritten to-do list with only the first few items crossed off.
img.frame: List in the lower half; the tip in the space above.

text: A good day feels like a chance to catch up.
*That's the trap.* The bill shows up two days later.

img.shows: A half-finished chore: boxes in a garage, a mower on a half-cut lawn. No people.
img.frame: The unfinished job in the top half; copy over the lower half.

text: So I let my numbers set the limit, *not my mood.*
The app I built gives me a daily pacing budget. Link in bio. 🩵

img.shows: The Journal home: Outlook card and the pacing strip, 1h 21m left of 3h 35m, ahead of pace.
img.frame: Pacing strip level with the copy.

music.notes: Same sound family as tips #1 and #2. A touch more thoughtful on slide 2, where the trap lands.

creatives.name: Tip 4: sit down for it
creatives.title: POTS tip #4: sit down for the things you always stand for
creatives.goal: Fourth single tip. Cheap, practical, and it leads straight into upright time.
creatives.caption: POTS tip #4. Nobody hands out medals for standing at the sink 🩵 Not medical advice, ask your doctor what's right for you. #pots #potstips #dysautonomia #pacing #spoonie

text: POTS tip #4:
*Sit down* for the things you always stand for.

img.shows: A plain stool at a kitchen counter or sink. No people.
img.frame: Stool in the lower half; the tip sits in the space above it.

text: Showering. Cooking. Brushing my teeth.
Standing still is *the hard part.* A stool gives those minutes back.

img.shows: A bathroom sink with a toothbrush, or a pan on a stove. No face.
img.frame: Subject in the top half; copy across the darkened lower half.
